title: Egypt's Largest Obelisk Trapped in Bedrock ⛏️
hook_sentence: Deep inside an ancient quarry in Aswan, the largest obelisk ever attempted remains trapped in solid bedrock.
narration_script: Deep inside an ancient quarry in Aswan, the largest obelisk ever attempted remains trapped in solid bedrock. Workers burned and wedged away upper rock, carving trenches where visible tool marks and ochre lines still mark their cuts. Surveys place its length between roughly 137 feet (41.75 m) and 138 feet (42 m), with weight calculations ranging from nearly 1,090 tonnes to 1,168 tonnes. Work was abandoned after structural cracks and multiple fissures appeared. Modern engineering studies cannot confirm which extraction method was intended, or whether moving the monolith was within granite's structural limits. These deep fissures left Egypt's greatest monument forever anchored in the stone.
closing_sentence: These deep fissures left Egypt's greatest monument forever anchored in the stone.
caption:
Structural cracks stopped ancient Egypt's largest monument in its tracks. ⛏️

Commissioned during the New Kingdom, this colossal monolith was possibly ordered by Queen Hatshepsut for the Temple of Amun at Karnak. Archaeologists uncovered the titan in Aswan after it spent thousands of years buried under drifting sand. An unfinished obelisk base and ancient rock carvings discovered nearby confirm how intensively workers quarried this site.

Could ancient engineers have ever extracted a stone this massive, or was failure inevitable? 🏛️
